belief: If I forgive them, I'm saying what they did was okay.
origins: We often resist forgiveness because we fear it erases the wrong. If someone hurt us badly, forgiving can feel like letting them off the hook, minimizing our pain, or telling the world that their behavior is acceptable. Pressure from others to “just forgive” can strengthen the resistance.
teaches: Jesus said, “If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.” Forgiveness and rebuke go together, so forgiving is not saying it was okay. On the cross, Jesus prayed, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing,” though what they did was terrible. Paul writes, “Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath.” Forgiving means releasing the debt and leaving justice to God. It does not deny the wrong, and it does not require us to pretend.
self_statements: Forgiving them means it did not matter.
They will think they got away with it.
I would be dishonoring my pain.
Forgiveness means excusing what they did.
They have to answer for it first.
errors: Believing I must either excuse or hold a grudge.
Imagining that forgiveness cancels all consequences.
Assuming forgiveness will be taken as approval.
questions: What exactly do I think forgiveness would mean?
Can I name the wrong clearly and still forgive?
What would it mean to leave justice to God?
Did Jesus forgive without calling sin okay?
What are the consequences or boundaries that can remain?
What does holding on cost me?
truth: Forgiving does not say that what happened was okay. I can name the wrong, grieve it, and release the debt to God. Forgiveness frees me from bitterness; it does not erase accountability or require me to pretend.
hw_truths: I can name the wrong and still forgive.
Jesus forgave while the wrong was real.
log: Each week, write what happened plainly and one step of releasing it to God.
actions: Describe what happened with no minimizing.
List the things you do not have to do.
Pray, “I release this debt to You.”
Decide what limits will protect you.
prayer: Father, what happened was wrong. I bring it to You and release the debt. Give me freedom from bitterness without pretending, and leave justice with You. Amen.
hw_questions: What does forgiveness mean to me?
What do I release to God?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can name the wrong and still release it to God.”
